steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Eatwell Guide (2016) divides food into five groups: fruit and vegetables (at least 5-a-day), starchy carbohydrates (base of each meal), dairy and alternatives (moderate amounts), proteins (beans, pulses, fish, eggs, meat), and oils and spreads (small amounts).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Eatwell Guide applies to the overall diet, not individual meals. It shows the proportions of each food group that should be consumed over a day or week.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dietary Reference Values (DRVs) are estimates of the energy and nutrient requirements for different population groups. They include EAR (Estimated Average Requirement), RNI (Reference Nutrient Intake), and LRNI (Lower Reference Nutrient Intake).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: RNI is the amount of a nutrient sufficient for almost all individuals in a population group. If intake falls below LRNI, deficiency is likely.
